findings.title: Requery after a cache miss still uses the stale cached folder tree
findings.body: When cached perms don't allow the request, Check refetches permissions from the DB and calls checkPermission again. For resources with folder support, checkPermission calls checkInheritedPermissions, which goes through buildFolderTree and reads the cached folder tree (30s TTL). If a user creates a folder, then a subfolder or dashboard inside it, the refreshed permissions include the new parent folder scope. The cached tree does not contain the new folder, so tree.Ancestors does not find the ancestor. The check is denied, and the denial is then cached for another 30s. The PR's stated goal (creators can access what they just created) is therefore only partly met for nested resources. The folder tree should be refreshed on the requery path as well.

findings.title: Negative cache entries are written for resources that may not exist yet
findings.body: Every deny is cached for 30s under a key of user, action, name and parent folder. If a check for a dashboard or folder runs before its permissions exist (for example a pre-creation or race check by the creator), the denial is cached. The creator then gets denied for up to 30s after creation, because the denial check at line 117 runs before any DB requery. This reintroduces the bug the PR is meant to fix. Nothing invalidates the entry on permission or resource creation.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous and shares the permission cache key prefix
findings.body: The denial key is namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. It reuses the `.perm_<uid>_<action>` prefix of userPermCacheKey, so the two entry types live in the same keyspace. Because name and parent are joined with a plain `_` and UIDs can contain underscores, different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key, for example ("a_b","c") and ("a","b_c"). A denial for one resource could then wrongly deny another. A distinct prefix such as `.perm_denial_` and an unambiguous separator would avoid this.

findings.title: Deny-cache test does not prove the denial entry short-circuits the check
findings.body: The test comment says the permCache entry is set to "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the value is `false`. A false scope would produce a deny even if the denial cache were ignored. The test also falls through to the fake store, which has no permissions, so it would pass without the feature. No test covers the denial cache being populated after a DB-confirmed deny, or a denial entry expiring and permissions being requeried. The value should be `true`, and a populate-on-deny test should be added.
